title: Lazy drive sync is a Proposed ADR, not shipped behaviour: today opening a remote drive still streams every document's history from timestamp zero
content:
ADR 0001 is marked **Status: Proposed** (2026-07-16, decider acaldas, "Implements: TBD"), so nothing in it describes current behaviour. What it describes is the problem and a design.

The problem: Connect eagerly syncs an entire drive on connect. Opening a remote drive on a Switchboard reactor streams the **full operation history of every document from timestamp 0** and replays it locally. Two costs follow — a cold load proportional to the whole drive regardless of what the user looks at, and **no prioritization**, so the document the user actually opened has no priority over the thousands they never touch.

The proposed design is lazy sync built on the sync protocol (explicitly *not* on the fetch/GraphQL document subgraphs, which would introduce a second divergent read path), opt-in, with minimal Connect changes: sync the drive document first because it lists its children, then sync a document's operations when it is opened; opening waits for that initial sync and is writable afterwards.

Two facts constrain any alternative and are worth remembering independently of the ADR. The **sync cursor is per-channel, collection-wide and forward-only**, so a live channel's filter cannot be widened to backfill a document whose operations predate the cursor. And a document's operation log is reachable **only through a collection it belongs to** — `operation-index.find` inner-joins on `document_collections`.

The ADR targets the legacy `powerhouse/document-drive` model, whose node list can diverge from `document_collections`.
